For duty one, the tracker write, I would have recorded task T-4 as landed on the relay/T-4 branch and merged to main at commit 8ba7db7, with a short note on what changed: the NFC-normalization fix in slugify so per-character transliteration runs against a normalized string instead of raw Unicode input. The tracker entry should point at the commit and the underlying bug (transliteration silently dropping or mishandling characters that weren't in composed form) rather than restating the diff, since the commit itself is the durable record of what changed.

For duty two, the compound judgment, I judged this as worth capturing because the root cause wasn't visible from reading the slugify function in isolation. Per-character transliteration logic looks correct on its own; the defect only shows up when you know Unicode text can arrive in multiple equivalent but differently-encoded forms, and that normalizing first is a precondition the code didn't previously enforce or document. That's exactly the kind of seam, a contract the code depends on but doesn't state, that a future session or reviewer would get wrong again without a note explaining why NFC-normalize-first matters here. It isn't a case where the fix speaks for itself in the diff, so recording the reasoning separately was the right call.
